sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ pramukhataḥ kṛtvā bhagadattaṃ ca māriṣa evam eṣa kṣayo vṛtto rājan durmantrite tava
english: Setting Bhīṣma and Bhagadatta at the forefront, good sir — thus, O king, has this destruction come to pass, all through your evil counsel.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā gateṣu śūreṣu teṣāṃ mama ca saṃjaya kiṃ vai bhīmas tadākārṣīt tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the heroes on their side and on mine had thus fared, Saṃjaya, what then did Bhīma do? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca viratho bhīmaseno vai karṇavākśalyapīḍitaḥ amarṣavaśam āpannaḥ phalgunaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Bhīmasena, his chariot broken and stung by the barbed words of Karṇa, fell into the grip of fury and spoke this word to Phalguna.

sanskrit: punaḥ punas tūbaraka mūḍha audariketi ca akṛtāstraka mā yodhīr bāla saṃgrāmakātara
english: Again and again he taunted me — 'Beardless oaf, fool, glutton, untrained in arms, do not fight, you child, you coward of the battlefield!' —

sanskrit: iti mām abravīt karṇaḥ paśyatas te dhanaṃjaya evaṃ vaktā ca me vadhyas tena cokto 'smi bhārata
english: thus did Karṇa speak to me before your very eyes, Dhanaṃjaya. He who speaks so to me deserves death at my hands, and by him have I been so addressed, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etad vrataṃ mahābāho tvayā saha kṛtaṃ mayā yathaitan mama kaunteya tathā tava na saṃśayaḥ
english: This vow, O mighty-armed one, I have taken together with you; as this is my charge, son of Kuntī, so is it yours — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tadvadhāya naraśreṣṭha smaraitad vacanaṃ mama yathā bhavati tat satyaṃ tathā kuru dhanaṃjaya
english: For his slaying, O best of men, remember this word of mine; so act, Dhanaṃjaya, that it be made true.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya bhīmasyāmitavikramaḥ tato 'rjuno 'bravīt karṇaṃ kiṃ cid abhyetya saṃyuge
english: Hearing that word of Bhīma's, Arjuna of measureless valour drew a little closer in the battle and spoke to Karṇa.

sanskrit: karṇa karṇa vṛthādṛṣṭe sūtaputrātmasaṃstuta adharmabuddhe śṛṇu me yat tvā vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam
english: Karṇa, O Karṇa, vain in your seeing, charioteer's son who praises only himself, mind set on unrighteousness — hear from me now what I shall tell you.

sanskrit: dvividhaṃ karma śūrāṇāṃ yuddhe jayaparājayau tau cāpy anityau rādheya vāsavasyāpi yudhyataḥ
english: Twofold is the fortune of heroes in war: victory and defeat. And both are uncertain, Rādheya — even for Vāsava when he fights.

sanskrit: mumūrṣur yuyudhānena viratho 'si visarjitaḥ yadṛcchayā bhīmasenaṃ virathaṃ kṛtavān asi
english: When you were near death at Yuyudhāna's hands, your chariot wrecked, you were spared and let go; and only by chance did you make Bhīmasena chariotless.

sanskrit: adharmas tv eṣa rādheya yat tvaṃ bhīmam avocathāḥ yuddhadharmaṃ vijānan vai yudhyantam apalāyinam pūrayantaṃ yathāśakti śūrakarmāhave tathā
english: But this was unrighteous, Rādheya, that you spoke so to Bhīma — one who knows the law of war, who fights and does not flee, who fulfils to the utmost of his power a hero's work in the fray.

sanskrit: paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ keśavasya mamaiva ca viratho bhīmasenena kṛto 'si bahuśo raṇe na ca tvāṃ paruṣaṃ kiṃ cid uktavān paṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Before the eyes of all the armies, of Keśava and of me, you were made chariotless by Bhīmasena many a time in battle, yet the son of Pāṇḍu never spoke one harsh word to you.

sanskrit: yasmāt tu bahu rūkṣaṃ ca śrāvitas te vṛkodaraḥ parokṣaṃ yac ca saubhadro yuṣmābhir nihato mama
english: But because you made Vṛkodara hear much that was cruel, and because Subhadrā's son was slain by you all in unfair fashion —

sanskrit: tasmād asyāvalepasya sadyaḥ phalam avāpnuhi tvayā tasya dhanuś chinnam ātmanāśāya durmate
english: for that arrogance reap now its instant fruit. You cut his bowstring to your own undoing, O evil-minded one.

sanskrit: tasmād vadhyo 'si me mūḍha sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ kuru tvaṃ sarvakṛtyāni mahat te bhayam āgatam
english: Therefore you, fool, are to be slain by me, together with your servants, your forces, and your steeds. Do all that you must do — a great terror has come upon you.

sanskrit: hantāsmi vṛṣasenaṃ te prekṣamāṇasya saṃyuge ye cānye 'py upayāsyanti buddhimohena māṃ nṛpāḥ tāṃś ca sarvān haniṣyāmi satyenāyudham ālabhe
english: I shall slay your Vṛṣasena before your watching eyes in the fight; and whatever other kings shall come at me through delusion of mind, them too shall I slay, all of them — by truth I lay hand upon my weapon.

sanskrit: tvāṃ ca mūḍhākṛtaprajñam atimāninam āhave dṛṣṭvā duryodhano mando bhṛśaṃ tapsyati pātitam
english: And when dull Duryodhana sees you — fool of unripe wit, overweening — struck down in battle, he shall grieve bitterly.

sanskrit: arjunena pratijñāte vadhe karṇasutasya tu mahān sutumulaḥ śabdo babhūva rathināṃ tadā
english: When Arjuna had vowed the slaying of Karṇa's son, a great and tumultuous clamour rose then among the chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: tasminn ākulasaṃgrāme vartamāne mahābhaye mandaraśmiḥ sahasrāṃśur astaṃ girim upāgamat
english: While that confused and dreadful battle was raging, the thousand-rayed sun, its beams grown faint, drew near the mountain of setting.

sanskrit: tato rājan hṛṣīkeśaḥ saṃgrāmaśirasi sthitam tīrṇapratijñaṃ bībhatsuṃ pariṣvajyedam abravīt
english: Then, O king, Hṛṣīkeśa embraced Bībhatsu, who stood at the battle's head, his vow fulfilled, and spoke thus to him.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā saṃpāditā jiṣṇo pratijñā mahatī tvayā diṣṭyā ca nihataḥ pāpo vṛddhakṣatraḥ sahātmajaḥ
english: By good fortune, Jiṣṇu, your great vow has been accomplished by you; and by good fortune the wicked Vṛddhakṣatra is slain together with his son.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ prāpya devasenāpi bhārata sīdeta samare jiṣṇo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: Even an army of gods, Bhārata, on meeting Dhṛtarāṣṭra's host would sink in the battle, Jiṣṇu — of this there can be no doubt.

sanskrit: na taṃ paśyāmi lokeṣu cintayan puruṣaṃ kva cit tvad ṛte puruṣavyāghra ya etad yodhayed balam
english: Though I ponder it, I see nowhere in the worlds, O tiger among men, any man but you who could do battle with this force.

sanskrit: mahāprabhāvā bahavas tvayā tulyādhikāpi vā sametāḥ pṛthivīpālā dhārtarāṣṭrasya kāraṇāt te tvāṃ prāpya raṇe kruddhaṃ nābhyavartanta daṃśitāḥ
english: Many guardians of the earth of great might, equal to you or greater, gathered for Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son's sake; yet, meeting you wrathful in battle, mailed though they were, they could not stand their ground.

sanskrit: tava vīryaṃ balaṃ caiva rudraśakrāntakopamam nedṛśaṃ śaknuyāt kaś cid raṇe kartuṃ parākramam yādṛśaṃ kṛtavān adya tvam ekaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Your prowess and your strength are like those of Rudra, Śakra, and Yama. No one could perform in battle such a feat as you alone have done this day, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: evam eva hate karṇe sānubandhe durātmani vardhayiṣyāmi bhūyas tvāṃ vijitāriṃ hatadviṣam
english: Even so, when the evil-souled Karṇa is slain with all his kin, I shall exalt you the more — conqueror of your enemies, slayer of your foes.

sanskrit: tam arjunaḥ pratyuvāca prasādāt tava mādhava pratijñeyaṃ mayottīrṇā vibudhair api dustarā
english: To him Arjuna replied: By your grace, Mādhava, this vow has been carried through by me — a vow hard to cross even for the gods.

sanskrit: anāścaryo jayas teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ nātho 'si mādhava tvatprasādān mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ saṃprāpsyati yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: No wonder is victory for those whose lord you are, Mādhava. By your grace Yudhiṣṭhira shall gain the whole earth.

sanskrit: tavaiva bhāro vārṣṇeya tavaiva vijayaḥ prabho vardhanīyās tava vayaṃ preṣyāś ca madhusūdana
english: Yours alone is the burden, Vārṣṇeya, yours alone the victory, O lord. We are yours to raise up and yours to command, slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ smayan kṛṣṇaḥ śanakair vāhayan hayān darśayām āsa pārthāya krūram āyodhanaṃ mahat
english: Addressed thus, Kṛṣṇa, smiling, gently driving the horses on, showed to Pārtha that vast and cruel field of battle.

sanskrit: śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca prārthayanto jayaṃ yuddhe prathitaṃ ca mahad yaśaḥ pṛthivyāṃ śerate śūrāḥ pārthivās tvaccharair hatāḥ
english: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: Craving victory in war and far-famed glory, the heroes and the kings lie upon the earth, slain by your shafts.

sanskrit: vikīrṇaśastrābharaṇā vipannāśvarathadvipāḥ saṃchinnabhinnavarmāṇo vaiklavyaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ
english: Their weapons and ornaments scattered, their horses, chariots, and elephants undone, their armour cleft and shattered, they have come to utter ruin.

sanskrit: sasattvā gatasattvāś ca prabhayā parayā yutāḥ sajīvā iva lakṣyante gatasattvā narādhipāḥ
english: The living and the lifeless alike, endowed with surpassing radiance — these lords of men, though life has fled, seem still as though alive.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śaraiḥ svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śastraiś ca vividhaiḥ śitaiḥ vāhanair āyudhaiś caiva saṃpūrṇāṃ paśya medinīm
english: Behold the earth filled with their gold-feathered arrows, their many sharp weapons, their mounts and their armaments.

sanskrit: varmabhiś carmabhir hāraiḥ śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ uṣṇīṣair mukuṭaiḥ sragbhiś cūḍāmaṇibhir ambaraiḥ
english: With cuirasses, with shields, with necklaces, with heads still bearing their earrings, with turbans, diadems, garlands, crest-jewels, and garments —

sanskrit: kaṇṭhasūtrair aṅgadaiś ca niṣkair api ca suprabhaiḥ anyaiś cābharaṇaiś citrair bhāti bhārata medinī
english: with necklets and armlets and bright gold ornaments, and with other gleaming jewels of every kind, the earth shines, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: cāmarair vyajanaiś citrair dhvajaiś cāśvarathadvipaiḥ vividhaiś ca paristomair aśvānāṃ ca prakīrṇakaiḥ
english: With yak-tail whisks, with gay fans, with banners, with horses, chariots, and elephants, with coverlets of many sorts, and with the fly-whisks of the horses —

sanskrit: kuthābhiś ca vicitrābhir varūthaiś ca mahādhanaiḥ saṃstīrṇāṃ vasudhāṃ paśya citrapaṭṭair ivāvṛtām
english: with richly patterned elephant-housings and with costly chariot-guards — behold the earth strewn over, as though robed in figured cloth.

sanskrit: nāgebhyaḥ patitān anyān kalpitebhyo dvipaiḥ saha siṃhān vajrapraṇunnebhyo giryagrebhya iva cyutān
english: Behold others fallen from their elephants — those caparisoned beasts — together with the elephants themselves, like lions tumbled from mountain peaks struck down by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: saṃsyūtān vājibhiḥ sārdhaṃ dharaṇyāṃ paśya cāparān padātisādisaṃghāṃś ca kṣatajaughapariplutān
english: Behold yet others sewn to the ground along with their horses, and the throngs of footmen and riders awash in floods of blood.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evaṃ saṃdarśayan kṛṣṇo raṇabhūmiṃ kirīṭinaḥ svaiḥ sametaḥ sa muditaḥ pāñcajanyaṃ vyanādayat
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus showing the field of battle to the Diademed One, Kṛṣṇa, joined by his own and filled with joy, sounded the conch Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā rathād āplutya bhārata paryaṣvajat tadā kṛṣṇāv ānandāśrupariplutaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, leaping down from his chariot, O Bhārata, embraced the two Kṛṣṇas, overflowing with tears of joy.

sanskrit: pramṛjya vadanaṃ śubhraṃ puṇḍarīkasamaprabham abravīd vāsudevaṃ ca pāṇḍavaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam
english: Wiping his bright face, radiant as a white lotus, he spoke to Vāsudeva and to the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā paśyāmi saṃgrāme tīrṇabhārau mahārathau diṣṭyā ca nihataḥ pāpaḥ saindhavaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ
english: By good fortune I behold you both, great chariot-warriors, your burden in battle crossed; and by good fortune the wicked lord of Sindhu, basest of men, is slain.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa diṣṭyā mama prītir mahatī pratipāditā diṣṭyā śatrugaṇāś caiva nimagnāḥ śokasāgare
english: By good fortune, Kṛṣṇa, my great gladness has been brought to pass; and by good fortune the hosts of foes are plunged into an ocean of grief.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ duṣkaraṃ kiṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate sarvalokagurur yeṣāṃ tvaṃ nātho madhusūdana
english: For those whose lord you are, the teacher of all the worlds, nothing in the three worlds is hard to achieve, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: tava prasādād govinda vayaṃ jeṣyāmahe ripūn yathā pūrvaṃ prasādāt te dānavān pākaśāsanaḥ
english: By your grace, Govinda, we shall vanquish our foes, even as of old, by your grace, the Chastiser of Pāka overcame the Dānavas.

sanskrit: pṛthivīvijayo vāpi trailokyavijayo 'pi vā dhruvo hi teṣāṃ vārṣṇeya yeṣāṃ tuṣṭo 'si mādhava
english: Conquest of the earth, or even conquest of the three worlds, is assured, Vārṣṇeya, for those with whom you are pleased, Mādhava.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ vidyate pāpaṃ saṃgrāme vā parājayaḥ tridaśeśvaranāthas tvaṃ yeṣāṃ tuṣṭo 'si mādhava
english: For them there is no sin, nor defeat in battle, whose lord is you, the lord of the lord of the thirty gods, with whom you are pleased, Mādhava.

sanskrit: tvatprasādād dhṛṣīkeśa śakraḥ suragaṇeśvaraḥ trailokyavijayaṃ śrīmān prāptavān raṇamūrdhani
english: By your grace, Hṛṣīkeśa, glorious Śakra, lord of the hosts of gods, won the conquest of the three worlds at the head of battle.

sanskrit: tava caiva prasādena tridaśās tridaśeśvara amaratvaṃ gatāḥ kṛṣṇa lokāṃś cāśnuvate 'kṣayān
english: And by your grace, O lord of the thirty gods, the thirty themselves attained immortality, Kṛṣṇa, and enjoy imperishable worlds.

sanskrit: tvatprasādasamutthena vikrameṇārisūdana sureśatvaṃ gataḥ śakro hatvā daityān sahasraśaḥ
english: By a prowess sprung from your grace, O slayer of foes, Śakra attained lordship over the gods, having slain the Daityas by the thousands.

sanskrit: tvatprasādād dhṛṣīkeśa jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam svavartmani sthitaṃ vīra japahomeṣu vartate
english: By your grace, Hṛṣīkeśa, the world of moving and unmoving things abides each in its own course, O hero, and engages in muttered prayer and oblation.

sanskrit: ekārṇavam idaṃ pūrvaṃ sarvam āsīt tamomayam tvatprasādāt prakāśatvaṃ jagat prāptaṃ narottama
english: In the beginning all this was one ocean, wholly wrapped in darkness; by your grace the world attained to light, O best of men.

sanskrit: sraṣṭāraṃ sarvalokānāṃ paramātmānam acyutam ye prapannā hṛṣīkeśaṃ na te muhyanti karhi cit
english: They who have taken refuge in Hṛṣīkeśa — creator of all the worlds, the supreme Self, the unfallen — are never at any time deluded.

sanskrit: anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ lokakartāram avyayam tvāṃ bhaktā ye hṛṣīkeśa durgāṇy atitaranti te
english: They who are devoted to you, Hṛṣīkeśa — the god without beginning or end, the maker of the worlds, the imperishable — cross over all hardships.

sanskrit: paraṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇānāṃ paraṃ ca yat prapadyatas taṃ paramaṃ parā bhūtir vidhīyate
english: To him who takes refuge in the supreme Person, the ancient One, that which is highest among all things primeval, the highest prosperity is ordained.

sanskrit: yo 'gāta caturo vedān yaś ca vedeṣu gīyate taṃ prapadya mahātmānaṃ bhūtim āpnoty anuttamām
english: He who chanted forth the four Vedas, and he who is hymned within the Vedas — taking refuge in that great-souled one, a man attains a prosperity beyond all others.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayasakhā yaś ca dhanaṃjayahitaś ca yaḥ taṃ dhanaṃjayagoptāraṃ prapadya sukham edhate
english: He who is Dhanaṃjaya's friend and Dhanaṃjaya's good — taking refuge in that guardian of Dhanaṃjaya, a man thrives in happiness.

sanskrit: ity uktau tau mahātmānāv ubhau keśavapāṇḍavau tāv abrūtāṃ tadā hṛṣṭau rājānaṃ pṛthivīpatim
english: Thus addressed, those two great-souled ones, Keśava and the Pāṇḍava both, then spoke gladly to the king, the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tava kopāgninā dagdhaḥ pāpo rājā jayadrathaḥ udīrṇaṃ cāpi sumahad dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ raṇe
english: By the fire of your wrath the wicked King Jayadratha has been consumed; and the surging, vast host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son in battle —

sanskrit: hanyate nihataṃ caiva vinaṅkṣyati ca bhārata tava krodhahatā hy ete kauravāḥ śatrusūdana
english: is being slain, is slain already, and shall perish utterly, O Bhārata; for these Kauravas are struck down by your anger, slayer of foes.

sanskrit: tvāṃ hi cakṣurhaṇaṃ vīraṃ kopayitvā suyodhanaḥ samitrabandhuḥ samare prāṇāṃs tyakṣyati durmatiḥ
english: For having angered you, a hero who slays with a mere glance, ill-minded Suyodhana, together with his friends and kinsmen, shall yield up his life in the fray.

sanskrit: tava krodhahataḥ pūrvaṃ devair api sudurjayaḥ śaratalpagataḥ śete bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ
english: Struck down before by your wrath, Bhīṣma the grandsire of the Kurus, hard to conquer even by the gods, lies upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: durlabho hi jayas teṣāṃ saṃgrāme ripusūdana yātā mṛtyuvaśaṃ te vai yeṣāṃ kruddho 'si pāṇḍava
english: Hard to win is victory in battle for those, O slayer of foes; truly they pass into the power of death with whom you are wrathful, Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ prāṇāḥ priyāḥ putrāḥ saukhyāni vividhāni ca acirāt tasya naśyanti yeṣāṃ kruddho 'si mānada
english: Kingdom, life, beloved sons, and pleasures of every kind — soon do these perish for those with whom you are wrathful, O giver of honour.

sanskrit: vinaṣṭān kauravān manye saputrapaśubāndhavān rājadharmapare nityaṃ tvayi kruddhe yudhiṣṭhira
english: I deem the Kauravas already destroyed, with their sons, their cattle, and their kin, now that you, ever devoted to the duty of kings, are wrathful, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhuḥ sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ abhivādya guruṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ mārgaṇaiḥ kṣatavikṣatau sthitāv āstāṃ maheṣvāsau pāñcālyaiḥ parivāritau
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīma and the great chariot-warrior Sātyaki, having saluted their elder and superior, those two great bowmen stood gashed and torn by arrows, encircled by the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭva muditau vīrau prāñjalī cāgrataḥ sthitau abhyanandata kaunteyas tāv ubhau bhīmasātyakī
english: Beholding those two heroes glad before him, standing with hands folded in reverence, the son of Kuntī rejoiced over them both, Bhīma and Sātyaki.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā paśyāmi vāṃ vīrau vimuktau sainyasāgarāt droṇagrāhād durādharṣād dhārdikyamakarālayāt diṣṭyā ca nirjitāḥ saṃkhye pṛthivyāṃ sarvapārthivāḥ
english: By good fortune I behold you, heroes, delivered from the ocean of armies — from the unassailable Droṇa-crocodile, from the lair of the sea-monster Hārdikya; and by good fortune all the kings of the earth are vanquished in the fight.

sanskrit: yuvāṃ vijayinau cāpi diṣṭyā paśyāmi saṃyuge diṣṭyā droṇo jitaḥ saṃkhye hārdikyaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: By good fortune I behold you both victorious in the battle; and by good fortune Droṇa is overcome in the fray, and the mighty Hārdikya as well.

sanskrit: sainyārṇavaṃ samuttīrṇau diṣṭyā paśyāmi cānaghau samaraślāghinau vīrau samareṣv apalāyinau mama prāṇasamau caiva diṣṭyā paśyāmi vām aham
english: By good fortune I behold you, blameless ones, crossed safely over the ocean of armies — heroes glorious in battle, never fleeing the fight; and by good fortune I behold you both, who are dear to me as my own breath.

sanskrit: ity uktvā pāṇḍavo rājā yuyudhānavṛkodarau sasvaje puruṣavyāghrau harṣād bāṣpaṃ mumoca ha
english: Having spoken thus, the Pāṇḍava king embraced Yuyudhāna and Vṛkodara, those tigers among men, and for very joy let fall his tears.

sanskrit: tataḥ pramuditaṃ sarvaṃ balam āsīd viśāṃ pate pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaṃ dṛṣṭvā yuddhāya ca mano dadhe
english: Then, O lord of peoples, the whole army of the Pāṇḍavas was filled with delight, and beholding their victory set its mind upon the battle still to come.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saindhave nihate rājan putras tava suyodhanaḥ aśruklinnamukho dīno nirutsāho dviṣajjaye amanyatārjunasamo yodho bhuvi na vidyate
english: Saṃjaya said: When the lord of Sindhu was slain, O king, your son Suyodhana, his face wet with tears, wretched and bereft of hope of conquering his foes, thought that there was no warrior on earth equal to Arjuna.

sanskrit: na droṇo na ca rādheyo nāśvatthāmā kṛpo na ca kruddhasya pramukhe sthātuṃ paryāptā iti māriṣa
english: Neither Droṇa, nor Rādheya, nor Aśvatthāman, nor Kṛpa was able to stand before him in his wrath — so he thought, good sir.

sanskrit: nirjitya hi raṇe pārthaḥ sarvān mama mahārathān avadhīt saindhavaṃ saṃkhye nainaṃ kaś cid avārayat
english: For Pārtha, having vanquished in battle all my great chariot-warriors, slew the lord of Sindhu in the fight, and none could turn him back.

sanskrit: sarvathā hatam evaitat kauravāṇāṃ mahad balam na hy asya vidyate trātā sākṣād api puraṃdaraḥ
english: In every way this great host of the Kauravas is already as good as slain; for it has no protector — not even Purandara himself in person.

sanskrit: yam upāśritya saṃgrāme kṛtaḥ śastrasamudyamaḥ sa karṇo nirjitaḥ saṃkhye hataś caiva jayadrathaḥ
english: He upon whom we leaned to raise our arms for battle — that Karṇa has been vanquished in the fight, and Jayadratha too is slain.
